_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present -a
entries.usage: Now or regularly, -a verbs.
entries.example: Eu vorbesc română.

entries.point: -ea, -e and -i verbs (a vedea, a merge, a dormi)
entries.label: Present -ea/-e/-i
entries.usage: Now or regularly, other verb classes.
entries.example: Merg acasă.

entries.label: Perfect compus
entries.usage: A finished past: am + participle.
entries.example: Am vorbit ieri.

entries.label: Imperfect
entries.usage: The ongoing or habitual past.
entries.example: Mă jucam mereu.

entries.point: The future (voi scrie / o să scriu)
entries.label: Future
entries.usage: What will happen.
entries.example: Voi mânca mâine.

entries.label: Conditional
entries.usage: What would happen.
entries.example: Aș vrea să plec.

entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: After să — wish, purpose.
entries.example: Vreau să vii.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: Commands.
entries.example: Scrie mai tare!

entries.label: A fi (to be)
entries.usage: Saying what someone or something is.
entries.example: Eu sunt student. — I am a student.

entries.label: A avea (to have)
entries.usage: Saying what you have — and how old you are.
entries.example: Eu am douăzeci de ani. — I am twenty years old.

entries.label: Irregular presents
entries.usage: The everyday verbs that refuse the pattern: want, can, know.
entries.example: Eu vreau o cafea, te rog. — I want a coffee, please.

entries.label: Reflexive verbs
entries.usage: Actions you do to yourself: wash, wake up, feel.
entries.example: În fiecare dimineață mă trezesc la șapte. — Every morning I wake up at seven.

entries.point: The passive voice (este scris / se vinde)
entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: When what happened matters more than who did it.
entries.example: Cartea este scrisă în limba română. — The book is written in Romanian.

entries.label: Pluperfect
entries.usage: Already over before another past moment: had done it.
entries.example: Când ai sosit, eu deja mâncasem. — When you arrived, I had already eaten.

entries.label: Past conditional
entries.usage: What would have happened, but never did.
entries.example: Aș fi venit imediat, dar nu am știut nimic. — I would have come at once, but I knew nothing.

entries.label: Gerund
entries.usage: One action going on alongside another: he left singing.
entries.example: A intrat în cameră zâmbind. — He entered the room smiling.

entries.point: The supine (de scris, ușor de făcut)
entries.label: Supine
entries.usage: Naming the job itself: something to write, easy to do.
entries.example: Am multe lucruri de făcut azi. — I have many things to do today.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: Saying not: nu sits straight in front of the verb.
entries.example: Eu nu vorbesc engleză. — I don't speak English.

entries.point: Este / sunt — there is, there are
entries.label: There is / are
entries.usage: Saying what exists somewhere — Romanian just uses to be.
entries.example: Pe masă este o carte. — There is a book on the table.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: Passing on what someone else said, asked or told you.
entries.example: Mi-a spus că va întârzia puțin. — He told me that he'll be a bit late.

entries.label: Dacă-clauses
entries.usage: If this, then that — the likely and the imagined.
entries.example: Dacă înveți mult, vei reuși la examen. — If you study a lot, you'll pass the exam.

entries.point: Subjunctive after impersonals (trebuie să, e posibil să)
entries.label: Trebuie să
entries.usage: After must, it's possible, it's good — what follows takes să.
entries.example: Trebuie să plecăm acum, e târziu. — We must leave now, it's late.

entries.label: Connectors
entries.usage: Although, because, so that — joining clauses in careful speech.
entries.example: Deși era târziu, am continuat discuția. — Although it was late, we continued the discussion.

entries.point: Register & the literary layer (perfectul simplu, formal style)
entries.label: Literary register
entries.usage: The written past and formal wording you meet in books.
entries.example: Se făcu liniște, iar el merse încet spre ușă. — Silence fell, and he walked slowly to the door. (literary past)

entries.point: The definite article is a suffix (-ul / -a)
entries.label: Definite suffix
entries.usage: The article attaches to the noun end.
entries.example: băiat → băiatul

entries.label: Genitive-dative
entries.usage: of / to — one case for both.
entries.example: cartea băiatului

entries.label: Plural
entries.usage: Noun plural forms.
entries.example: băiat → băieți

entries.label: Adjectives
entries.usage: Adjectives match gender and number.
entries.example: o casă mare

entries.point: Gender and number — including the neuter
entries.label: Gender (incl. neuter)
entries.usage: Masculine, feminine, and the Romanian neuter.
entries.example: un scaun, două scaune

entries.label: Subject pronouns
entries.usage: I, you, he — usually left out, added for emphasis.
entries.example: Eu sunt din București. — I am from Bucharest.

entries.label: Un / o
entries.usage: Saying a or an; the choice announces the gender.
entries.example: Am un câine. — I have a dog.

entries.point: Direct object pronouns (mă, te, îl, o…)
entries.label: Direct object pronouns
entries.usage: Me, him, her, it — a short word before the verb.
entries.example: Ce carte bună! O citesc acum. — What a good book! I'm reading it now.

entries.label: Dative pronouns
entries.usage: Who you give or say something to — and what you like.
entries.example: Îmi place foarte mult muzica. — I really like music. (music pleases me)

entries.label: Possessives
entries.usage: My, your, our — after the noun, and matching it.
entries.example: Mașina mea este nouă. — My car is new.

entries.label: This / that
entries.usage: Pointing at the one here or the one over there.
entries.example: Această carte este interesantă. — This book is interesting.

entries.label: Case prepositions
entries.usage: Saying thanks to, because of, in front of — the word after them changes shape.
entries.example: Am reușit datorită ajutorului tău. — I succeeded thanks to your help.

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: Asking where, what, when — the question word leads.
entries.example: Unde locuiești? — Where do you live?

entries.label: În, la, cu, pe
entries.usage: In, at, with, for — and the ending the noun drops after them.
entries.example: Merg la școală în fiecare zi. — I go to school every day.

entries.label: Mai … decât / cel mai
entries.usage: Saying bigger than something, and the biggest of all.
entries.example: Bucureștiul este mai mare decât Iașiul. — Bucharest is bigger than Iași.

entries.point: Comparative structures (tot atât de, din ce în ce)
entries.label: As … as
entries.usage: Two things equal, or one getting more and more so.
entries.example: El este la fel de înalt ca mine. — He is as tall as me.

entries.label: Relative care
entries.usage: Hanging a describing clause on: the man who came.
entries.example: Bărbatul care a venit este medic. — The man who came is a doctor.

entries.point: Clitic doubling (pe Ion îl văd, îi dau Mariei)
entries.label: Doubling with pe
entries.usage: Whenever you name the person you see or give something to, Romanian says the short pronoun as well — it isn't optional.
entries.example: Pe Ion îl văd în fiecare zi. — I see Ion every day.
